beats.idea: Familiar coinage coexists with presidency differences

beats.idea: 1835 law creates uniform legal tender

beats.template_note: appear stamped Currency Act of 1835 scroll beside matching rupees across British India outline; show_text standard design and single legal tender; give payment from payer to recipient; accept payment on accepted with qualifier कानून के नियमों से.

beats.idea: Uniformity is not decimalisation; identify 1835 correctly

beats.template_note: compare matching coins with decimal division diagram using ≠ on नहीं; show_text original 1835 issue: William IV on a portrait-free coin issue label; accept that label; refuse Queen Victoria issue label on final नहीं. No ruler portraits.

beats.template_note: appear rupee to sterling to gold link arrows, sterling-gold link marked conditional; refuse direct domestic rupee-to-gold redemption arrow on नहीं; appear fluctuating silver-price chart leading to Fowler Committee recommendation document at 1898, labelled recommend rupee–gold link. No physical gold payout.

beats.idea: Distinguish recommendation, implementation and illustrative rate
beats.shows: 1898 recommendation → 1899 implementation; reserves support exchange link.
beats.template_note: Show 1898 and late-1890s implementation, especially 1899, on the timeline; mark ₹10 per £1 as illustrative, not historical. Reserves and policy support the exchange-link diagram; चलाने names a general requirement, not a new payment process.

beats.idea: Monetary chronology has three distinct dimensions

beats.template_note: appear each milestone in spoken order, connected by timeline arrows: silver Rupiya, Mughal mint, Company coins, 1835 uniformity, 1861 note monopoly, gold-exchange reforms, RBI. beats.idea: Silver discoveries increased supply and depressed prices

beats.template_note: appear silver deposit at discoveries; appear additional silver at extra silver; meter silver-price tag downward at prices गिरे, without numerical values. Add a 1873–1947 bracket labelled Silver Crisis / Gold-exchange era when spoken; mark discoveries late nineteenth century.

beats.idea: Weaker silver means more rupees per foreign payment

beats.idea: Historical relationship, not historical example quantities

beats.template_note: Static evidence-versus-illustration comparison: discovery and falling silver-price symbols under Historical relationship; kg and price placeholders under Illustration—not actual data. Extra silver beside the illustrative tags explains supply pressure without replaying a process.

beats.idea: Recall the complete silver-to-gold-link causal chain

beats.template_note: Reveal connected nodes in spoken order: appear silver deposit; appear growing silver supply; show downward silver-price indicator; compare rupee with foreign-payment symbol using a strain mark; appear gold linked to the rupee, labelled जरूरत. Present the final link as a need, not an enacted policy transaction.

book_pictures.title:
Period | Nature of the Rupee
Eight chronological rows

beats.idea: Market pricing with RBI shock management
beats.shows: Market arrows move rupee; RBI cushions fluctuations.
beats.template_note: Highlight the table’s 1993 onwards row. Parts: appear rupee and exchange-rate graph; move rupee downward on 'depreciation', labelled foreign value; appear demand and supply arrows feeding the graph on 'demand–supply'; move RBI institution beside the fluctuating graph on 'RBI'; transform sharply fluctuating graph into a gentler fluctuating graph on 'झटके सँभाल सकता है', retaining movement rather than fixing a rate. Show fixed-rate commitment as a locked horizontal rate line, then refuse it on 'न'; show unmanaged float as an unbuffered fluctuating graph, then refuse it on the second 'न'.

beats.idea: ₹ identifies the rupee, not new money
beats.shows: ₹100 tag enlarges ₹; script elements combine.
beats.template_note: Parts: appear price label bearing ₹100; move an enlarged copy of ₹ beside the unchanged tag on '₹'; compare symbol and rupee with an identity link, labelled 'written पहचान', rather than creating a second currency. Show the credit 'D. Udaya Kumar' as text only. Show '2010' beside the symbol on '2010'. Appear Devanagari and Roman script elements in separate slots, then move them into an enlarged ₹ construction diagram. Use script-form highlights, not a claim that two complete letters simply join.

beats.idea: Chronology links distinct monetary changes
beats.shows: Milestones align; redemption, exchange price, reserves separate.
beats.template_note: Parts: appear a numbered sequence of independence flag, decimal subdivision diagram, changed gold-link diagram, managed-float graph and ₹ symbol, cued by their respective spoken terms; connect these to corresponding book-table rows without adding unsupported dates. Then compare two panels: fiat currency with a crossed gold-redemption link under 'redemption', and managed-float graph with foreign exchange price under 'foreign price'. On 'gold reserves रह सकते हैं', appear gold reserves alongside fiat currency without reconnecting the redemption link. This shows reserve holdings can coexist with fiat status.

beats.idea: One rupee, different subdivisions
beats.shows: Equal rupee strips; old subdivisions beside modern hundredths.
beats.template_note: Static comparison: old strips show 1 Rupee = 16 Annas = 64 Paise = 192 Pies; modern strip shows 1 Rupee = 100 Paise.

beats.idea: Equal value does not mean equal count
beats.shows: Equal-length strips gain different numbers of divisions.
beats.template_note: Keep four strips equal in length, each tagged ₹1. Parts in order: appear four undivided strips; transform the first into 16 equal sections on '16', second into 64 on '64', third into 192 on '192', fourth into 100 on '100'; compare the old and modern strips with '=' and labels 'same value' and 'different subdivision counts'. Use fine ticks with enlarged detail, not coin piles.

beats.idea: Old pice are not modern paise
beats.shows: 1957 separates strips; highlighted old/new units differ.
beats.template_note: Show old and new strips across a 1957 divider. Enlarge one section from each: 'old paisa / pice = ₹1/64' versus 'modern paisa = ₹1/100', joined by ≠. No conversion process is enacted.

beats.idea: Decimal clarity is not increased purchasing power
beats.shows: ₹1.25 splits; purchasing-power meter stays unchanged.
beats.template_note: Parts: appear an amount strip tagged ₹1.25; transform it into adjoining ₹1 and 25 modern paise segments, with the latter one-quarter of the former; show_text above them '1 rupee + 25 paise'. On 'अपने-आप', appear a purchasing-power meter with a fixed pointer and label 'No automatic increase'. Do not introduce an annas–pies conversion or imply that purchasing power can never change.

beats.idea: Derive old units; isolate modern hundredths
nouns: old paisa subdivided into three pies
beats.shows: Old units group and subdivide; modern hundredths separate.
beats.template_note: Parts: appear the old ₹1 strip with 64 sections; transform it into 16 outlined groups of four sections; show_text '64 ÷ 16 = 4 old paise per anna'. Appear an enlarged old paisa; transform it into three pie sections; show_text '192 ÷ 64 = 3 pies per old paisa'. Appear a separate modern ₹1 strip with 100 divisions; show_text on one highlighted section 'modern paisa = ₹1/100'. Keep the modern panel visually isolated.

beats.idea: Dollar demand raises the importer's bill
beats.shows: Demand rises; quote and importer’s bill rise.
beats.template_note: Show importer facing bank with dollars and rupees; show_text quote ₹80/$ and $100 bill ₹8,000. At demand बढ़ी, raise demand meter; change quote to ₹84/$ and bill to ₹8,400. Move ₹8,400-tagged rupees from importer to bank and $100-tagged dollars back.

beats.idea: RBI dollar sales soften the quote
beats.shows: RBI sells dollars; rupees return; quote softens.
beats.template_note: Place banks inside foreign-exchange market. Move dollars from RBI to banks and raise supply meter; move rupees back to RBI. At same मानो show a conditional tag; lower quote ₹84/$ to ₹82/$ and $100 bill ₹8,400 to ₹8,200. Retain ₹8,000 as a distinct initial reference, not the outcome.

beats.idea: Smooth volatility, not fix the rate
beats.shows: Rate swings soften; fixed-rate line crossed out.
beats.template_note: Compare sharp rate swings with smaller but continuing swings, marking smoothing as the aim. At नहीं cross out a separate fixed-rate line. Move dollars from RBI into supply, raise supply meter, and shrink upward pressure arrow to connect sales with reduced pressure.

beats.idea: No guaranteed rate or automatic ₹84 trigger
beats.shows: Demand lifts rate; automatic ₹84 trigger crossed.
beats.template_note: Raise demand-pressure meter and reveal a possible upward rate path, tagged सकता है. At नहीं cross out guarantee stamp. Highlight excessive swings as the intervention condition. Show ₹84 trigger marker beside RBI and cross out its automatic-trigger connection at नहीं; do not show a sale being triggered.

beats.idea: Dollar sales ease market pressure
beats.shows: Demand rises; RBI dollars enter market; pressure falls.
beats.template_note: Ordered parts: appear dollar demand meter; meter upward on 'बढ़ी'; meter dollar price upward on 'महँगा'; appear dollars beside RBI institution on 'RBI'; move dollars from RBI into foreign exchange market with sale tag on 'बेचे'; meter dollar supply upward on 'supply बढ़ी'; meter exchange-rate pressure downward on 'pressure घटा'. Connect stages with arrows; use no invented amounts.

beats.idea: Smoothing is not a fixed-rate commitment
beats.shows: Smaller fluctuations versus fixed line; market with intervention.
beats.template_note: Ordered parts: appear two matched exchange-rate charts; transform large fluctuations into smaller, still-varying fluctuations on 'झटके घटाता'; show a horizontal rate line in the fixing chart on 'fixing', with 'तय rate की commitment' as its short label on 'commitment'; compare charts with ≠. On 'साथ', appear foreign exchange market beside RBI intervention, joined with +; retain the varying smoothing chart above both to show coexistence without a fixed-rate promise. Charts are schematic, with no invented values.
